STEP 1 - Vessel type: The food sits on a white square-ish flat plate with a rim band and flat centre, no inner wall. Flat plate.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type: square plate, likely 20-30 cm. The plate looks medium-large relative to the side salad plate on the left (about 18-20 cm), so this plate is roughly 25 cm across.
b) Reference: the side salad plate on the left is about 20 cm wide. The main plate is about 1.3 times wider than that, giving about 26 cm.
Final width: 26 cm (square), area about 676 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Caesar salad (romaine with dressing and croutons): covers roughly 45% of the plate, about 300 cm². Mound averages about 2 cm thick. Volume-based estimate: 300 × 2 × 0.5 ≈ 300 ml at light density. Use bulk density for dressed greens about 0.5 g/ml, giving about 150-160 g. Raw-ish leafy greens with dressing: estimate 150 g.
- Crumbed fish fillet (top right): about 60 cm² footprint, about 1 cm thick, so about 60 ml of fish at density 1.0, giving about 60 g. Breaded fish is fairly dense, so use 70 g.
- Brown/glazed meat piece with orange zest (right): about 70 cm² footprint, about 1.5 cm thick, average 0.7 cm, giving about 50 ml; at density 1.0 that is about 60 g. Estimate 70 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No obvious base layer under the fish or meat beyond the plate surface. Croutons are part of the salad, already counted. No extra hidden layer added.

STEP 5 - Energy density (as served):
- Caesar salad with dressing and croutons: about 190 kcal per 100 g (dressing and croutons add energy).
- Breaded fried fish: about 220 kcal per 100 g.
- Glazed meat with zest: about 200 kcal per 100 g.

Totals: salad 150 g → 285 kcal; fish 70 g → 154 kcal; meat 70 g → 140 kcal. Total about 580 kcal, 290 g of food.
